utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. First of all, I hope, General Galic, that you were properly informed about what happened yesterday, because I can imagine that if you are in detention, that the information takes more time to get to you. And on the other hand, I also can understand that especially under these circumstances, even -- especially if you would not know exactly what would happen, that it's an even more unpleasant experience than it is for everyone else in this building.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I was informed sufficiently about what happened yesterday. I have to tell you that the information actually circulated very quickly in detention. That's what they say. I don't know whether that's true. This is my first imprisonment, and thank you very much. And I will follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then before we proceed to examine the witness, I'd like to bring a few issues to the attention of the parties. I notice, Mr. Stamp, that Mr. Ierace is not there, but I assume that you can -- because these are not issues specific for the witness to be examined at this moment. First of all -- and I am addressing now especially the Prosecution -- there is some confusion as to some protective witnesses, and that is also the reason, Madam Registrar, why I would ask you to see whether it would be possible to be in private session just for two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not in private session any more. We are in open session now. I have not been attentive enough to immediately change to open session once we dealt with the protection of witnesses. I raised that the Chamber would like to pay attention to a request of the Defence for Trial Chamber's order in relation to material evidence filed on the 5th of March, 2002. And I immediately went to the requests made by the Defence. It's clear to the Chamber now that as far as the tail-fin is concerned, the expert can inspect it as soon as the expert is in The Hague. There still remains the problem of the shrapnel being available. That relates, among other things, to paragraph 6 of the motion, which reads: "The attempts of a witness, Sead Besic, on hearing out the 4th of March 2002 tried to explain that some pieces of mines and grenades are lost or through is unacceptable." Let's try to put the question in objective terms. Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution at this moment, is shrapnel or any other part of the projectile in the custody or under the control of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that it might be difficult at this very moment to give an order to the Prosecution to allow your expert to inspect part of this projectile. Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution seeking to get control -- to get in its custody or under its control any other elements of this projectile?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We are, Mr. President, and have been for some time. And if we are ultimately successful, then of course we will notify the Defence. But so far, we have been unable to obtain any pieces of shrapnel that relate to that incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you think that the -- does the Prosecution need the assistance of the Chamber by any order, or is it not a matter of unwillingness as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there have been requests made of the relevant authorities, and our understanding is that those authorities are cooperative, have been cooperative. The issue is simply whether those pieces can be located. And at this stage, it appears they cannot by those authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you inform the Chamber immediately once they have been located, and when there's any fair expectation that they could become in your custody or under your control.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you like to respond briefly on that or...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you for raising this question, first of all. I think that we can say that the interventions were made by the Prosecution towards the authorities in Sarajevo, that is, that one fragment, that is the tail-fin, the stabiliser, was given, was delivered, was handed over. Now, we have to know when did the Prosecution also intervene for the other fragments, to ask for the other pieces of shrapnel, and also, Mr. President, what was the reply of the Bosnian authorities? That is, the authorities in Sarajevo. This is a very important point because this is a very important proof and very important piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever ask the Prosecution when they applied for it and what the answer was? Because -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when I last -- last time I asked about these elements, this was the session that we had with Mr. Ierace and Mr. Mundis, and Mr. Waespi as well as the case manager, and I said exactly which elements this concerned. I did not have a clear answer at the time. So we did not see these fragments. We didn't know about these fragments, when we could see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, after we heard the answer, which is more or less in line of what has been said by the Prosecution before, that is, that these smaller pieces could not be located, that also was the testimony of Mr. Besic as far as my recollection goes. Now you tell us that we should know exactly when the Prosecution asked for the other parts and what the answer was. My question to you was whether these specific questions have been asked by you to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which specific question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The two questions I just mentioned on which you'd like to have an answer, that is, when the Prosecution asked for these smaller parts of the projectile, and what answer was given by the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will see in a moment in the file whether we did ask these questions. But so far, Mr. President, we did not know that these items were not available, all of them. So I do not believe that the question was asked in this form to start with. However, I will ask my colleague to see whether there is something in the file. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I can say is the following: Now, to give you an element in my answer, now this is very important, Mr. President, because if we have these photographs, these pieces of shrapnel, that means that we can legitimately believe that these photographs were in the file of the Prosecution. That means the Prosecution has them. Not every time that there is a photograph we are going to ask whether the Prosecution has or does not have these pieces. Now, if these pieces were photographed and they are part of the Prosecution case, then we must assume that they exist and they are somewhere -- that the Prosecution does have them, that we have the right to examine them. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, apart from perhaps slowing down a bit for the interpreters, I have to establish at this moment that the Prosecution says we have not in our custody, nor under our control, those pieces of which, it seems to us now, I was not aware of that there are photographs taken of those pieces. Just from a distance it looks very much as one of the laboratory photographs made in Sarajevo, because they are using the same type of measuring. You say they should be in the hands of the Prosecution. The Prosecution says they are not. So there we have a problem. It's a bit difficult perhaps at this moment to give an order to give an opportunity to inspect the smaller parts when the Prosecution says that they do not have it in their custody or under their control. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, just to give you an indication because I believe this is important, we have here a document which was given to us by the Prosecution, and the number is 0026-8383, and the following, 0026-8383, that is what I just said, and the next one, which is a document containing various photographs as well as the stabiliser fin. The stabiliser, and immediately afterwards in the order the various bits of shrapnel. So when we are given all these elements dated 1994, we have absolutely no reason to believe that these elements do not exist or they no longer exist. We never asked the Prosecution when they will want us to ask for these pieces from the Sarajevo authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let me just try to understand you correctly. It is the point of the Defence at this moment that the shrapnel pieces still do exist and are kept away from the Defence. Is that, in short, your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, I do not know whether they still exist. This could be the case; it could have been the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That will then have to be sorted out by either party in the way I do understand the Prosecution is seeking to have it located in Sarajevo. And of course, if the Prosecution says they are not able to locate it in Sarajevo, it's up to the Defence to come up with convincing arguments or even evidence that it can be located and it can be produced. Of course, this Chamber at this moment cannot say whether it exists or not. If I order one of the parties to bring it into this courtroom, that would be an impossible exercise. Let's then for the tail-fin, it's clear; for the shrapnel, it's not clear yet, and I cannot clarify it at this moment. And I urge the parties to do their utmost best to clarify where the shrapnel is. Then, we come to point B. If I understand the Defence well, the Defence seeks that the directive and orders of the ABiH main staff towards its corpses as well as the order of the 1st Corps command toward Brigades in its composition will be disclosed to the Defence. Is that what I understand you said, to submit for the defence, but you want to have it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have the first question to Mr. Ierace. Are the directives and orders sought by the Defence, are they in the custody or under the control of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution does not claim to have all of the orders that were issued by the ABiH in the relevant period. This issue has been a subject of much correspondence between the parties since February of last year when the Defence first made this request. In essence, the nature of that correspondence has been to reach some argument as to what was relevant. The initial request was far too broad. At a meeting with the Defence approximately six weeks ago, the Defence told us that they had reason to believe that the Office of the Prosecutor possessed orders which it had not yet handed over. In support of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you a very clear question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any of these documents mentioned by the Defence, is there any document that is either in the custody or control of the Prosecution that has not been disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Not that we are aware of at this stage, but we are doing a check and I anticipate we will have the results of that check by the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let's then wait and see what the Prosecution will find in this check. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well, Mr. President. As soon as this check is positive, and I don't doubt, then I hope we shall return to this question because these elements could already give us some crucial elements in the case of this important witness, and I know that the Prosecution does have in its hands some of the elements. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say that you know that there is something in the hands of the Prosecution that the Prosecution at this moment is not aware of, and you're certain that they will come up with a positive answer by the end of this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not even the end of this week. I do not know that. But I know it because we had a meeting with Mr. Ierace and other learned friends, and we know that there is important topographic material, I'm referring to the topographic material which allows us to localise certain matters that of course the Prosecution check whatever they like, but the Defence simply does not have that. And this is a fact which I believe the Prosecution cannot deny, cannot challenge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait until the end of this week and see what the result is of the check by the Prosecution. And if then the answer of the Prosecution is not satisfactory to the Defence, of course they will be in a position to convince the Chamber that the answer is not a correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Mr. President. But I say these elements directly affect the cross-examination which in turn is important for some of the very important witnesses like the one we are expecting today. And I am saying that we asked for these materials some weeks ago. We still do not have it. I am speaking it very clearly which will be very important for the hypothetical and possible appeal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This would mean, I would suggest, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you think on one of the witnesses being cross-examined by the Defence that you are convinced that you have not a material you could expect soon from the Prosecution at the end of the final check, that you then indicate so, so that we'll not finally perhaps not excuse the witness but we might decide then that if your expectation turns out to be a correct one, that then there might be an opportunity to recall the witness for further cross-examination. But if you'd then please indicate so, so that we can -- are aware of that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I shall be very happy to do so. And I wish to be precise: In order for us to be able to examine these maps, we cannot do it on the spot because they are not like tourist maps. They are very specialised maps, and we need a military expert --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever they turn up, maps or whatever documents not disclosed earlier to the Defence, of course we'll take proper care that the Defence has the opportunity to prepare itself for the -- for cross-examining the witness to whom these -- to whom's testimony these material relates. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned colleague has now twice referred to the material in dispute being maps rather than orders. The document filed this morning refers only to orders. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do see so. I must be honest that I did not check every single number mentioned in one of the letters attached to it. So at this moment, I'm hesitant to say that among these orders or attached to these orders or connected to these orders there could be no maps. But that's one of the things I would say if there's any misunderstanding about that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin will be quite happy to explain why he's using the word "maps" in this courtroom while he is talking about directive and orders as well as orders toward brigades in its composition. Of course, orders can be accompanied by maps explaining the orders. But I'm not quite sure. But may I invite you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you are not doing it over. You are quite right, as you have said. We are talking about maps, of course, and equally about orders. But very often, the orders refer to maps, that say such and such element, such and such line, such and such strategic objective, and then it refers to maps which were in the file. There are maps of the main staff which are of utmost importance as to know what happened in their time and place. Therefore we are talking about the maps, therefore the different maps including the orders. I believe that the Prosecution understood it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I nevertheless remind you that it would be better to clarify this directly to Mr. Ierace during one of the breaks to come, because even if an order would relate to geographical positions, and if the order would be in the custody or under the control of the Prosecution, this would not automatically mean that the map showing such geographical positions is also in the custody or under the control of the Prosecution. So would you please sort out that during -- well, yesterday we had a lot of breaks. But to sort this out in such a way that confusions and misunderstanding is avoided when the Chamber is informed by the end of this week. So I think now we dealt with Item B as well. I'll now go to Item C. Item C says to submit to the Defence all audiotapes with intercepted talks of General Stanislav Galic if it is in the possession of such tapes. From the request the Defence made, I did understand but let's just first verify it, that the Prosecution said that they were not in possession of any audiotapes of intercepted talks of General Galic. May I just first ask, Mr. Ierace, are there any audiotapes of intercepted conversations of General Galic in your custody or under your control which have not been disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the next question: Is the Prosecution aware of the existence of such audiotapes, although not in the custody or under the control of the Prosecution itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We have no such knowledge, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the Prosecution ever sought to establish the existence of such audiotapes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has made inquiries as to whether there are any such tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And to date has been unsuccessful in obtaining any such tapes or indeed establishing if any exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I first wanted to establish the factual basis of your request. You've heard the answers. If there's any reason why you say that these answers are unsatisfactory, please inform the Chamber. But then perhaps not right on the spot, but if you think you can do it in one or two minutes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Formally we are satisfied with this answer regarding this particular item. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Then there is another -- the Chamber is informed that you have submitted the request for Visas for expert witnesses. This would mean that there's -- I hope at least that there's a fair chance that the Prosecution can fulfill your request to have objects inspected by your experts on as short as possible notice. So that is not at this moment something we should discuss further.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. At this stage I must say that this is not so much a matter for the Prosecution because we see that, concretely speaking, the shrapnel is not here, and besides this object is no longer in the possession of the Prosecution, but the Registry. Because it has now become -- so it has been transferred to the Registry, and I believe now it is a matter for the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think not yet, as a matter of fact. But it might be soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know that you don't want to engage into debate but I really must say that it has never been considered by the, nor has it ever been the case, that the Prosecution, at an earlier time, had the shrapnel. Whilst I'm on my feet, might I raise one other matter very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we do it after I finish the whole request, then I'll give you an opportunity for that. Because the next request is that the Defence suggests that the Trial Chamber should enable expert witnesses of the Defence to be present during examination of expert witnesses of the Prosecution. I think there has never been any request that reached the Chamber whether or not to allow an expert witness of the Defence to be present during the examination of an expert witness of the Prosecution. So as soon as such a request is addressed to us, we'll, of course, on shortest notice inform you about our decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much, Mr. President. We simply merely to inform the Chamber what we shall do when the technical problem arise, or rather what we would like to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. And the whole issue of experts I'll spend a few minutes on that as well. Then finally, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you informed us that the evidence you presented, especially I'm referring to page 583 and a few other pages, concerning information from the UN has as its source annex 6 to the final report. I'm quite happy that you could confirm what I thought it would be, although I would prefer that next time you come up with a source primarily and only not just confirm my feelings about it. But let's -- so we have dealt with I think the major aspects of the request made by the Defence on the 5th of March. Mr. Ierace, there was another issue. And I tell you that as far as it concerns expert witnesses, I'll pay some attention to it also. I don't know whether it's about expert witnesses or not. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will meet the Defence at 3.45. I assume that is our next break, pursuant to your suggestion. Last week the Trial Chamber directed that the Defence provide written submissions in relation to the application of Rule 90(H)(ii). There was not a timetable mentioned for that. We have not yet received any submissions. I'd be grateful if the Trial Chamber could indicate a date by which the Defence and then the Prosecution is to do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first ask what the intention as far as time is concerned of the Defence is. You'd make written submissions on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe I understood that would be following the decision that you will take, your Chamber will be happy to hear what the parties have to say. But it is not a matter of any major importance. I believe the Defence is now trying to concentrate on the evidence and exhibits. We are not connected to the internet, so if there is a certain delay which is very long, then yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what time you expect to provide the Chamber with your written submissions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will comply with your decision, as always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you left it to us, although I would have gladly perhaps accepted suggestions from your side, I would say within ten days would be fair in our view. And I keep in mind that you had already a couple of days to think about it. Yes, any other issue, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. All I want to do is ask a question which I presume will be asked during this case, and that is the need to inform the Defence earlier, that is, prior to the seven days' deadline, when the experts will be examined so that we could communicate with our experts and so that they could arrive in The Hague in time. It could pose a technical problem, so we would simply like to ask our learned friends to tell us well in advance when the experts will be coming so that we could contact our experts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic, as I indicated, and you seem to have similar problems as I have on this issue, I would spend some more time to the expert witnesses. The list provided by the Prosecution to the Chamber, the list pursuant to Rule 65 ter is not always clear as to whether a witness will testify as a normal witness or as an expert witness. It is, for example, quite clear in respect of Mirza Sabljica, because he is indicated as an Expert Witness, capital letters. But for other witnesses are described as experts in specific fields, but then usually in the body of the summary of the statement itself, there you find that there's some specific expertise. If you'd like to have a copy of the names, I'll be glad to provide it to you later, this concerns the witness Hamel, artillery expert; Higgs mortar expert; Philips, military expert; Turner, psychiatrist, an expert in trauma; expert, Robert Donia, expert in Balkan history and affairs. So there we find some expertise in the summary of the statement. For some other witnesses, it is also unclear whether they will be called as expert witnesses or not. For example, if we look at Witness AD, the witness is presented as having acquired expertise on shelling and sniping, crime site investigations. So it's not clear whether they come and testify as experts or mainly as witnesses on specific investigations. Although it's indicated that he'll come notably to validate his report. We have similar questions as far as Witness Cekic, who is a professor of political science and specialised in research and crimes against humanity. This concerns Isnet Ceric, who is head of psychiatry of the university medical centre and an author. Another problem with the Rule 65 ter witness list is that it mentioned some unidentified expert witnesses, for example a sniping insert on page 1403, or a statistic expert, an artillery witness, a ballistic physicalist, another ballistic expert. When you need the pages, the Chamber of course will be glad to provide them to you. And the last I mentioned is an expert on command and control. The Chamber would be very much pleased if some clarification could be made in respect of all this. And also to disclose the identity of the unidentified expert witnesses. I then turn, apart from these items that still have to be clarified, to the procedure under Rule 94 bis. According to Rule 94 bis, the Defence shall file a notice indicating whether it accepts the expert witness statement or it wishes to cross-examine the expert witness. And this should be done by the Defence within 30 days after the expert witness statement is filed. This is Rule 94 bis under (B). Under 94 bis (A), it says that the statements of -- reports of expert witnesses should be disclosed to the Defence, and it always has been my understanding that whatever statements or reports of expert witnesses were in the hands of the Prosecution, that they were disclosed to the Defence. Is this understanding correct, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When the Prosecution intends to call the witness, then of course the Prosecution must provide a copy of that report to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But we have two different things. I think we have first of all the disclosure under 94 bis under (A) Which talks about disclosure, and then we have filing the report under 94 bis, under (B). Am I right in assuming that for all those expert witnesses, or witnesses that could be considered to be expert witnesses, that the Prosecution intends to call, that all the statements or reports, if available, have been disclosed at least, perhaps not filed, but disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: They have not, Mr. President. There's two categories of witnesses that you have identified. The first are those in respect of whom there are 65 ter summaries. And it's unclear to the Trial Chamber whether they are being called as experts or not. That is a simple matter for us to respond to, and I'll do it in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The second category are those that are unnamed. At the time that the -- we collide with Rule 65 ter, the old 94 bis rule applied, and that did not require the Prosecution to even refer to its expert witnesses until a relatively short period before it intended to call them. So we provided that information although we did not have to so as to better present some idea of the scope of the Prosecution case. Since that time, we have identified experts in most of those categories. And they are in the process of preparing their reports. And when they are completed, they will be disclosed and filed so as to comply with the new rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because the Chamber noticed that until now, I think only the report of Dr. Donia has been filed and the report of Mr. Higgs has been filed. For example, if, for example, Mr. Sabljica is in the -- on the list clearly identified, it was the one and only I mentioned, as an expert witness on the Rule 65 ter list, if I'm well informed, or -- because he will be called soon, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it might save time if I get back to you on Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And indeed the others that you have named.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Let's not spend time on it at this moment. You'll understand what our concern is, the concern of the Chamber is that if reports are not yet disclosed, if they are filed just shortly before the witness is called, then of course the Defence must have an opportunity to discuss these reports with their experts in order to prepare either for a notice saying that they would accept it or for cross-examination. And if we look at the time which should be granted and the time the Defence has to file a notice of whether accepting or wishing to cross-examine the witness, then we should clearly keep in mind that this cannot be done just shortly before calling the expert witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is an issue that perhaps I should raise at this stage. Some of the experts who you have identified will be required by the Prosecution to give evidence in relation to material which has come from the Defence, in particular, orders and other documents which one would assume have come from the archival material of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. That material has come to us in batches, the most recent batch approximately eight weeks ago. And I'm told by Mrs. Pilipovic that we can expect more. It takes some time to translate those documents and then to incorporate them. They will be incorporated into reports by persons who are perhaps more properly described not as experts by as analysts. It is taking us some time to complete that process. And it is likely that even in relation to the material we have so far received, that those reports will not be ready until the closing weeks of the Prosecution case. The Defence has had singular success in locating orders and other documents which relate to the accused, which is mystifying to the Prosecution, because we are told that the archive no longer exists. The reason I mention that is simply to make the point that it is not as if the Prosecution can obtain that material from any other source and complete those analytical reports at an earlier time. I raise it at this stage, and because it will impact upon our ability to present all our evidence sequentially. There is a possibility that by the time we have called all of our other witnesses, our analysts, and therefore, for instance, the command and control expert, who will depended to some extent upon the analytical report, cannot be called without there being a break in the Prosecution case. Naturally, we are doing everything we can to avoid that. But the wording of the new Expert Witness Rule is not helpful to us because of the addition of this 30-day period. So Mr. President, I will keep you informed about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you like, I can respond to all but one or two of the names you have mentioned at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could do so, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Richard Philips is an analyst.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to find something to write.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Or perhaps more accurately I should say he will be giving an analysis which is dependent in part upon the documents from the Defence and in part on documentation obtained elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I assume that what you call an analyst is someone who does not primarily testify on facts, but on his interpretation of reports or whatever other thing presented to him, and I would rather then say that this is a -- I would rather call him an expert than a normal witness, although there's always a mixture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the reason I use the two different terms is simply to my mind an expert is entitled to give an opinion and that opinion may be based on training or experience or both. An analyst to my mind is someone who examines documents and essentially saves the Court time by distilling the material to some basic propositions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether there's not always an opinion involved. For example, what is the essence of a document, is a question we'll have not to answer on -- okay. Yes, you call him an analyst. Perhaps I should have stayed away from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's an issue that may be revisited. And the same could be said of Rick Butler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Dr. Turner is indeed an expert on the topic of terror. Robert Donia is an historical expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have received his report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I hesitate to go further at this stage, Mr. President. I'll get back to you on the other names. I could have pressed but I prefer to have some time in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps wouldn't it be a better idea if you just write down briefly your position as far as what kind of witness or expert it is, and give perhaps a very brief explanation so that everyone knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. First of all, I would like to thank the Prosecution very much indeed to tell us that we've had some singular success. Now, what I wanted to say, Mr. President, is that I believe that we have a small transcript problem, is that we will have a 94 -- in the Rule 94 bis, there will be a 90-day rule, and I believe that it's 14-day rule. Is that correct? I just wanted to make sure so that we don't have a quid pro quo situation. Could you please confirm because we are talking about new dispositions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You indicated that there might be a misunderstanding on what's in the rule. What's in the rule we all know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then it's only a technical problem. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last one of 94 bis says that the -- within 30 days of the filing of the statement of the expert witness or such other time as prescribed by the Trial Chamber the opposing party shall file a notice...so 30 days or whatever other time limit set by the Chamber. I think we went through all the issues I had in mind we had to discuss. And we'll on short notice also discuss the 92 bis. We're almost ready in preparing our questions to the parties for a hearing previous to giving a decision. Any other issue to be raised at this very moment? If there's not, then -- yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you'll allow us, the Defence would like to be given information, if that is possible, information from the Chamber, since our schedule was made to last until the 1st of April, 2002. Now, the situation of General Galic in detention is such that he has to tell one month ahead of a visit from his family. Now, we are interested to be given a schedule or a work schedule for March and April so that we know whether there's going to be a break so we can just have some idea about the time frame. Is it so far we're working until the 1st of April? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that we have -- the schedule is published until the 1st of April, and, Madam Registrar, knowing that you are dealing extensively with the Court calendars, is the schedule for the beginning of April in such a stage that you can give any information on it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The 1st of April is, according to our schedule, 1st of April is second Easter -- is Easter Monday, and the 2nd of April, the Trial Chamber is sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: But the schedule is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The schedule is available. That's first of all, and I think we have a break of one week somewhere in late April, but I think we indicated that before to the parties, we would have one week off in June, and also a week -- I'm not quite sure, but I think it was the end of April. Do you know when we stay in recess, Madam Registrar, which week the Galic case is not heard?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: According to my schedule, in April there is no recess, but there is one week in June. If you give me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's another week. We'll give you the information after the break. I'm not even asking if there's any other thing to be discussed and ask quickly to the usher if he could bring in the witness. That will takes one or two minutes more than usual because I thought it was not fair to have the witness to wait for 50 minutes on the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please excuse me, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Besic. Another day --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you expect to appear again in this Court, but it surprised us all yesterday. May I remind you that the fire may be extinguished, but you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave the day before yesterday at the beginning of your examination. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Besic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Our cross-examination of the previous day was stopped at a time when you told us that you arrived with your team at the site of the incident. You arrived at Markale. That was 30 minutes or 35 minutes, about quarter past 1.00 in the afternoon, you said that you arrived. Could you tell us whether the investigating judge came with you, because you said also the public prosecutor was with you at the time as well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The judge came about five minutes after we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the investigating judge who is conducting the investigation, did he tell you -- did he tell you personally what had to be done?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me personally, but we waited for his permission to start the work, and we know what that work entailed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you, as a criminal technician, you were not given a task by the investigating judge what you were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the reason is because this is just a criminal technician's analysis that is supposed to be done, an examination that's supposed to be done at the site of the incident. The only thing that's important is that the investigating judge gives his permission for the work to start, and this permission was given and we started to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, what was the first thing that you did when you were given the permission to start the work?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, was to photograph the site and to videorecord the site as we found it. Then to check and examine the site of the incident --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, just to be precise, you photographed the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recorded with a videocamera or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who and what is the name of the person who did the videorecording?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person was Zlatanovic. He worked as a photo technician in our office, and he also has the same course completed for criminal technicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from Mr. Zlatanovic who had the video camera, at the site of the incident at the time of the investigation, were there other people who were recording the site? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody except the police who was conducting the investigation was not present with the videocamera on the site. Perhaps from some distance it was possible to make a videorecording, a filming, but at the site of the incident, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are confirming here that Mr. Zlatanovic was the only cameraman who was a member of your team and who was filming the material for you?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After you told us that you photographed the site, my question is did you fix the traces?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we fixed the traces in a sense that we -- we processed the site of the -- the actual impact of the projectile, where the projectile landed. We photographed the site without marking the direction where the projectile came from and then also it is possible to see it in the documentation, the other photographs that we took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that you photographed the site where, according to you, the projectile landed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a sketch of the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not do a sketch of the site of the incident. As far as I can remember, I believe that it was Mirza Sabljica, the ballistic expert, who did the sketch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you say is that you did not measure, you did not take any measurements on the site where you located the projectile?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you determine or do you know whether Mr. Sabljica determined the standing position from which he would do the measuring, in relation to the place where you located the projectile and in relation to the stalls and the buildings that we saw on the video material?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it is possible to see in the video material and the photo file, there is a map of the town as I explained already, and that we established the north. That means that it was put on the place where the projectile landed. Then the north was established, and then with an arrow, it gives us the direction where the projectile came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from your team on that sketch that you say that Mr. Sabljica made it, did anyone from the team put in all the elements that were on the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the sketch is made, then you normally take a starting position, a location which is immobile, you fix it. We call it a fixed point. So according to this point, it is a kind of parameter for the sketch. In this case, it's probably the -- probably the corner of the rear part of the market that was taken as this fixed point, and according -- with the help of a 90-degrees angles, this is how we determined the direction where the projectile came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who established the fixed point?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. Probably it was Mirza Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us that Mr. Zlatanovic [sic] did the filming, was the material that we had the opportunity to see during the examination-in-chief by my learned colleague, is this the material filmed by him with that one camera?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the most authentic material that was recorded by Mr. Zlatan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us today that you took photographs of the site of the -- where the projectile landed. Could you tell us who found the stabiliser of the shell?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at the photographs that we saw, could you tell us how did you find it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was cleaning the place, the location, where the projectile landed, the body tissue, the blood, the soil, I came to the centre of the location where the projectile landed, and I then tried to just see whether there was any shrapnel from the ignition fuse because there's very often that there are still some parts of the ignition left. And then that's when I found the mortar shell tail which I then did not touch after that until the UN team came to the site of the incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us at the time when you arrived at the site of the incident, did you see any UNPROFOR personnel there? Were there any nearby?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived, there was nobody else from the UN. They arrived about quarter of an hour after we arrived. 10, 15 minutes, I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, until the UNPROFOR personnel arrived, what did you do with regard to securing the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are not in charge of securing the site. The securing of the site is done by the police station which is in that part of the municipality. In this case, this is the Stari Grad Police Station. So the site was secured by the police from the police station Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're telling us that when you found the stabiliser, the shell stabiliser, you then did not do anything else regarding the stabiliser until the UNPROFOR people came?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, since we had the opportunity to see it on the videorecording, who is the person who positioned those sticks in form of a letter T?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirza Sabljica positioned the sticks, and Hamdija Cavcic, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when these sticks were positioned, you said that they were positioned by Mr. Sabljica and Mr. Cavcic. Could you see the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us here and now that the positioning of the sticks, that there was no digging before the positioning of the sticks around the place where the stabiliser of the shell was?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except for cleaning of the body tissue, blood, and any debris that was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how did Mr. Sabljica and Mr. Cavcic, how were they able to position the sticks in the form of a letter T if they did not determine the angle and if they could not see the stabiliser? On the basis what have did they position the sticks?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question asks the witness about the mental process of Mr. Sabljica and Mr. Cavcic, how did they do something. It is known that Mr. Sabljica is a witness. That is something within his limit. The witness does not have to speculate about how different specialists contemplated what they should do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand what the objection of my learned colleague is in relation to the work. But we are here in a situation that we have here a witness who was present at the site during the events and who said that he found himself the place where the projectile landed, that nothing was done around this particular place, and that it was done by Mr. Sabljica and by Mr. Cavcic. Now, we believe that by cross-examining the witness here today, we can find relevant information for this incident. The witness precisely showed us on the video material, or we were able to see these sticks in the form of a letter T. Now my question was how were they able to position the sticks in the stabiliser could not be seen, and the witness just confirmed that the stabiliser could not be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, isn't it true that whether -- how they could have done it is not something to determine who has not done it. I mean, that's the -- the objection is not that he was not there and I don't think that the objection is against any part of the testimony until now. But how could this witness explain something what was in the mind of another witness? Perhaps before giving a final decision on the -- Mr. Besic, was it explained to you on the basis of what the other persons carrying out the investigation were able to put the sticks as they did it? Did they explain to you how they did it, on the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a team that often went to sites of incidents, so we worked as a team. And in this case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- did they explain to you on the basis of what exactly they positioned the sticks? Did they explain it to you or did they not explain it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would it be a suggestion to ask about what was explained to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Witness, could you tell us, please, whether Mr. Sabljica or Mr. Cavcic, did they explain to you on the basis of what they positioned the sticks in the form of a letter T?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to determine the direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment when they were positioning the sticks, were you present there on that place where they placed these sticks?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm for us, tell us, or perhaps give us a reply, whether at that time when they were placing it, whether you could see the stabiliser of the shell?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that the place where these sticks were in the form of a letter T, that this place was covered with -- as we saw it on the photograph. Is that correct? And that before these sticks were positioned, nobody was digging that part, nobody was cleaning?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you could find a suitable moment to have a break. Would this be the moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I did not explain to you before that we spent quite some time in the beginning on some legal issues. Now and then we have to pay attention to legal issues as well as to the facts that you're testifying about. I'd like to thank you for your patience, and I'd like to see you back in this courtroom at a quarter past 4.00. We adjourn until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just before I give you the opportunity to resume the cross-examination, the breaks will be in Week 18, which is Monday, the 29th of April until Friday, the 3rd of May; and also during Week 24, which is from Monday, the 10th of June, until Friday, the 14th of June. And I'd like to make one other observation, more specifically addressing at this stage of the proceedings, the Defence, may I remind you that you have been instructed by the Pretrial Judge, Judge Rodrigues, on the 8th of November, 2001, that if you would not accept the report of an expert witness, you should give the reasons why. And apart from that, as an alternative to requesting the expert witness to be cross-examined, that you also could present a report of another expert on the same issue, let's say a contra expertise. Having said this, please Ms. Pilipovic, proceed, unless there's anything. Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, Mr. President, if I could ask one special imposition of the Court if for perhaps about five minutes before we close the taking of evidence today or at any time at the convenience of the Court, I could be allowed to make some submissions to the Court or we could have a discussion in respect of the status of the witness, Mirza Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll spend the last five minutes of today's hearing to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please Ms. Pilipovic, then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you've told us that you discovered the place where the projectile had landed. Can you tell us, as you were clearing the ground, did you clear it enough for the stabiliser to become visible?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not clearing the crater itself, but outside the crater. We wanted to remove all of the debris, blood, and tissues, as I have already said, in order to identify traces or marks around the crater. Because it is on the basis of shrapnel marks in the asphalt one determines the direction from which the projectile had come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that these two sticks were placed on the basis of the direction of the position of -- position of shrapnel, that is of shrapnel markings in the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us this: Who collected these pieces of shrapnel, or did you at all?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the pieces were collected on the scene, and the firing pin was found in the crater. That is, after the stabiliser was taken out, parts of the firing pin were also discovered there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, the collection of shrapnel, you said you did that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take photographs of the collection of shrapnel, or was it videotaped?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was neither photographed nor videotaped because we were in short supply of this material. And all the collected pieces of shrapnel were photographed in black and white in the laboratory.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the Defence would like to show the witness two photographs which we received from our learned friends to see if Mr. Besic could identify them and confirm that these are, indeed, the photographs and the shrapnel that the gentlemen collected and photographed. Your Honour, we have two photographs. I made a sufficient number of copies of photograph 14. We marked it D60, and the second photograph is photograph number 15, and we marked it D61. Your Honour, the Defence copied these photographs from a file given us by our learned friends, photograph 14 is 0026-8397. And photograph number 15 is 0026-8398. These are for the witness. Your Honour, need we put D on each of these photographs, or will it suffice only if we put it on the first copy, that is D numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should mark them all so that whenever we have a copy, that we know immediately that it's D. I know that you're a bit spoiled, perhaps, by the Registrar who did it very often for you. I'm only too glad to see that you're taking the effort now by yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this literally is being done in Geneva. The stamp comes from Geneva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I do not see any stamp, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm saying that stamp is being prepared in Geneva, and as of the next week, we shall not be having any more problems of this kind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's great. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you have two photographs in front of you, number 14 and number 15. Are these the photographs of the shrapnel that you found and photographed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the pieces of shrapnel found on the site, and they were photographed in our laboratory, in our criminal investigation laboratory in the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then tell us how many pieces of shrapnel did you collect altogether?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I believe you said, and I stand to be corrected, but when asked by my learned friend during the examination in chief, when we're talking about the shrapnel which you found, can you bring them to The Hague, and you said that had you been asked to do that, you would have brought them. Will you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that these shrapnel in these photographs, you said that you filed them and put them in safekeeping in the police station, they are still there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I hope so because in 1996, in 1996, we redid this building because it had been hit by three rocket grenades. So in 1996, we redid the building, and because we had plenty of evidence brought from different outside investigations, many things were discarded. So that I hope -- I'm not sure, but I hope that this shrapnel is still somewhere on the premises of the crime laboratory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, when you made your statements, did you tell the OTP investigators when you turned these photographs over to them that on the police premises was also the stabiliser which you had brought here, that is, the grenade and these pieces of shrapnel which you had photographed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the projectile was in existence. We did not discuss the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to submit this shrapnel to the OTP investigators for inspection?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are confirming that this is shrapnel of a mine which fell on Markale, if I may put it that way?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Besic. Can you confirm and answer, how much later did UNPROFOR members arrive? I believe you said 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tape, photograph the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know what they were doing. Because what we wanted to do was to show them where the shell had landed and what was in the crater.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if UNPROFOR members performed any kind of recording after arriving at the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you, that is, answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what activities were taken by UNPROFOR members at the time of their arrival?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of their arrival on the site where the shell had landed, we showed them where the crater was and told them to try and clear the crater, because the stabiliser was in it. What they did, you can find in the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you were present all the while as the UNPROFOR members were digging that part to get out the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present there throughout, because we took that stabiliser, and I took it to the laboratory. The projectile was extracted by UNPROFOR members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm if that moment when you say the stabiliser was taken out, was that recorded?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not recorded because of the material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were present all of the while when the UNPROFOR members were taking out this. Can you tell us how deep were the tail-fins lodged in the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 10 to 15 centimetres from the upper surface, that is, I mean, the asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how thick was the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three, four centimetres maybe. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, you said that on the 6th of February, 1994, a team of experts went out to perform the expertise. And I believe it was -- you said it was Mr. Zecevic and Mr. Sabljica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if their measurements and preparation of the expertise was done with the stabiliser? That is, did they take the stabiliser again and take it back to the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer, since we saw in the recording how UNPROFOR members digging around the place, where you told them was the stabiliser, can you answer how did you discover the existence of the stabiliser since we see them digging out that part, that is, that part that they were digging was discovered. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct it was covered. But when I finished the activity of cleaning to identify the markings on the asphalt before the two [indiscernible] for the determination of direction were placed, I looked into the hole to see if there were any pieces of shrapnel in the crater, the firing pin. And then I saw that the stabiliser was wedged in there and then I stopped all activity until they came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are now confirming that you were cleaning this part where the stabiliser was until --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not clean the area where the stabiliser was. I did not touch the crater with anything rough. I only handled it with my hands. That is, I moved the earth a little bit just to see if there were any pieces there, and then I spotted the stabiliser, and I ceased doing anything around the crater. In the crater, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you confirm to us that the stabiliser was taken out by members of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who did they give the stabiliser to? You said to you and that you took it away. But whom did they give it to you?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They gave it to me. I took it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you tell us that you took both the stabiliser and shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, shrapnels, that was collected on the site, I found them more or less. And another colleague who worked with me. But the pieces of shrapnel from the hole, from the crater, and the stabiliser, I was the one who found them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, at what point in time did Mr. Sabljica and Mr. Cavcic establish -- determine the direction from which allegedly the mine came? Was it after they had seen the pieces? Are you telling us that they placed the sticks when they saw the markings of the pieces?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely when this was cleaned, then they placed these two -- these two sticks in the specific direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the direction was established before the stabiliser was taken out?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, when did Mr. Cavcic and Mr. Sabljica, when did they give their opinion as to their belief about the direction from which the mine had arrived?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly but it could be two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer, when did you write your report about the scene and your observations about it? What date?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I was on duty both on Friday and Saturday, I had Sunday as a day off. And I did my report on Monday, I mean the photo documentation and the criminal report and the sketch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you did your criminal report on Monday, and that was how many days after the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident happened on the 5th, on Friday, so it was the 5th, and the 6th were the Saturday. I believe the 7th was Sunday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- when compiling your report, did you have other reports, too, or did you do it only on the basis of your photographs and --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criminal methodology presumes photo documentation, sketch, and submit it all to the operations officers who performed the investigation on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will go back to your record, that is your report. Now I will ask you a few questions about the incident which happened on the 4th of February at Dobrinja about which you spoke during the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. examination-in-chief. Can you tell us who was -- who were members of the investigation team which went out to investigate on the 4th of February in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judge Zdenko Eterovic, crime technicians Samir Sazman.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter has missed the name.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then Mirza Sabljica, Zlatko Mededovic. And the operations officer from the office of the genocide department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the interpreter is indicating she missed a name. So if the witness could be asked to repeat the judge, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please give the name of the judge again. Sometimes this can be done later on, but could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zdenko Eterovic was the judge; ballistic experts Mirza Sabljica, and Zlatko Mededovic, and crime technicians Sead Besic and Samir Salman, and the operations officers from the office of the genocide, I can't give you the names now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were telling us that you were the only crime technician on the team.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and my colleague Samir Salman. Sorry, there was another colleague, Suad Dzumisic who was doing the videorecording.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the report on the criminal investigation on this site for that day, did you write that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The on-site investigation report at Dobrinja where two mortar shells fell killing nine persons, 20 severely wounded and 20 other casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the site where you were, did you make a sketch of the site, you?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not do the sketch of the site. It was Samir Salman who did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that two mortar shells fell. Did you, when investigating the site, find any pieces of shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a certain quantity of shrapnel was found. Where they are now, I could not say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in your report you noted that you had found these pieces of shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you submitted your report, when you've compiled your report, did you assign that report?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall now. I think I may have signed it, or perhaps it was my colleague Samir Salman who did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when a report like this is compiled about a criminal technical investigation of the site of the incident, is that report filed after all the other reports are examined, who are done by other people who carried out other tasks?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criminal technical investigation report is accompanied by a photo file. It accompanies other reports, and everything is then given -- added to the main report that is done by the investigating judge in this case, it was Judge Eterovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness the report about investigation of the scene of the incident so that the witness could identify the document for us, and then if he does do so, then perhaps he could give us some explanation. And then I would like to ask him some questions in relation to this, and we would then tender it as evidence. We also gave it from the Prosecution, and the number is 0026.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I can also submit copies to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I presume you prenumbered it D62.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once a Defence or Prosecution number has presented a document, we usually can see what is the ERN number. So that's not a...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as I said, 0026-8234.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that a report in the original language or with the...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the report is in the original language, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a translation available? I mean, has there ever been a translation provided to you, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this moment, I cannot reply, but I cannot find it in the documents. I cannot find the translation into English of this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if it has been provided to you. Is the Prosecution aware whether this report has been provided, has been disclosed to the Defence also in English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am not quite sure if it has been. I can't answer that question. What I could say is that we would probably have an English translation and would, if given time, be able to supply the Court with an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What to do? Because if -- my problem is two-fold: First of all, the translation of elements you will ask the witness to make observations about, and the second one is the context of those elements in relation to the report as a whole. How much time, do you think, Mr. Stamp, it would take you to find out whether a translation does exist?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It would take about 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 10 minutes. Ms. Pilipovic, would there be any other subject you could examine -- cross-examine the witness on to start with so that we are better able to...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, so we'll stay away from this document for a while. But as far as I understand, Ms. Pilipovic will come back to it. Mr. Usher, could you please for the time being return D62 to the Registrar. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
