utterances.text: Witness, you told us during the examination-in-chief, asked by my learned colleague in explaining the photographs that were given by the Prosecution to the Defence also?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask the Registry if the witness could be shown the photo file for the incident of the 2nd of February, 1994. And that is the Prosecution Number, Prosecution material that was shown during the examination-in-chief by my learned colleague, and these are photographs that go up to number 11. Sorry, the last number is 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Ms. Pilipovic, you're talking about the 2nd of February, 1994. Are you referring to P2262, which is about the 5th of February? Are we talking about the Markale or the other?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we're talking about Markale, the 5th of February. I don't know why it says the 2nd. It was the 5th of February. It is the photo file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, that's P2262, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before I ask you some questions about the photographs that you were giving explanations about, could you tell us, when did the names of streets change in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you whether that was in 1993 or 1994, or whether even in 1992. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you have a look at the photograph number 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you can please put the photograph on the ELMO so that we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, could you tell us, when was this place photographed, before the UNPROFOR arrived or after?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This place was photographed before the UNPROFOR arrived. The marking was done before the UNPROFOR arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to go back to photograph number 5. Mr. Besic, asked by my learned colleague, you said that you cannot see an arrow here.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us from which place was this photograph taken. If it's not a problem, we can go back to photograph number 4 so that you can give us on that photograph, photograph number 4, the place either of the building or from the direction that this photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This site was photographed on the side of this building. This was -- this was done by a man who was making uniforms for the police and the army, so the photograph was done from this side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us on photograph number 5, could you mark for us the place and the direction of the stabiliser and the position of the stabiliser and of the fins, the way that they were located?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot do it on this photograph, because it's a wide-angle photograph. But this is the place where the projectile fell. This is where the crater is. So I cannot give you an angle, and I cannot put an arrow in here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, the witness is indicating on the photograph number 5 under which it says a wide view of the market. Where there is an arrow showing the place where the projectile landed, the witness indicated a part which is located between the stalls a place where traces are visible, traces of clothes, that is of shoes and pieces of paper. We cannot be quite specific. And the witness indicated the place where the projectile landed. And the photograph number 5 the witness tells us is shown on photograph number 4, and a building of where the shop was where uniforms were made for the police and the army. This shop is called 22nd of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, on the photograph number 4, the building where you say it is from this direction that the place was photographed, you said that on the ground floor, there was a shop for making -- for sewing uniforms for police and army. Could you tell us what was the rest of the building used for? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I don't know what the rest was used for. I can just make a correction. This is the building where the shop called 22nd of December was located before the war, and this shop or this workshop made uniforms for the police and the army for the previous army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, thank you. Could you tell us on photograph number 4, could you explain for us the buildings we can see behind the stalls? We said that this was here down is a supermarket. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the building on the left where it says "Boritz Travnik," [phoen] What was this building used for? Was this a residential building, was this business premise, or something else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a residential building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this photograph you marked with an arrow a place where there was damage done to the building by an explosion of an indetermined projectile. Did you establish this?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On this occasion, nobody -- there was no casualty, so there was no investigation. And this arrow was precisely indicated here so that it would make it clear that this had nothing to do -- this damage had nothing to do with this particular projectile, this incident, so that we would know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea when this projectile was fired, this one here?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not do an investigation when this damage occurred?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you told us on photographs number 4 and 5, you told us from which direction the photograph was taken, photograph number 5 as well as number 4. I would like to ask you to go to back to photograph number 8 now. Could you tell us, from which direction was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This damage, the place where the projectile landed, was photographed from the direction which is the rear end of the supermarket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, what is the distance from the rear end of the supermarket to this place where the sticks -- these sticks make a T?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot quite tell you exactly, but I believe it could be 2 to 3 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, could you give us an answer as to whether the members of UNPROFOR, in relation to this incident, whether they made -- whether they filed a report, whether they made a report?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, whatever the UNPROFOR did, we had absolutely no access to it, neither reports, no records, nothing, no material. Whatever they did, they did it for themselves and they never, ever sent anything on to us, although on several occasions we did do work together where members of the UN were killed, but we never received any report or record from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you worked with them occasionally, so to speak, you worked on investigations where UN members were killed. Could you confirm for us, these were the only situations that you worked together with UNPROFOR members, when someone from the UN was killed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we worked together often. They came, for instance, to this incident when a large number of people was killed. That's when they came as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, how many times and how many incidents did you work with UNPROFOR members before this incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly. I couldn't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in which period did you conduct investigations together with UNPROFOR members when UNPROFOR members were killed? When was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Considering that you told us the years, 1993, 1994, 1995, could you perhaps situate for us the incidents as well? Could you identify them and describe them, where they happened, where these incidents, in which part of the town?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that was under the control of the BH army, in all these locations, we went and we did investigation tasks together. That was from Dobrinja, Alipasino Polje, Novi Grad, Novo Sarajevo, Centar, Old Town, all those areas that were all in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us an answer as to whether it was with UNPROFOR members or without them you conducted investigations of incidents that happened outside of the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not with UNPROFOR members; without them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when that was and which parts of town were in question that you did investigations in?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the question is not in relation to these two incidents, I'm not sure whether I have to answer, whether that's relevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I'm asking you about the relevant time. Since you said 1992, 1993, 1994, you said that you conducted investigations in areas that was under the control of the BH army. Now, I asked you whether you conducted investigations outside of this area, in the years 1992, 1993, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in 1992 because we were surrounded. But in 1993, we had a passage through the famous tunnel. So we occasionally we were able to offer our services to police stations that were outside of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you answer, these police stations outside of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Hrasnica, Tarcin, Konjic, Pazaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, on these occasions that you conducted investigations at, were these investigations following sniping incidents, shelling incidents, or what was the reason and obviously what were the consequences of these incidents outside of that happened -- or outside of the town that was under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only went to Hrasnica because of shelling, and to the other areas we went for completely different types of investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us for these other investigations, could you tell us what they were about?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To do with crimes, suicides, robberies, thefts, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us that these areas that you told us you had these types of investigations, could you tell us under whose control were these areas?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These areas were under the control of BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you went to these investigations, did you have any information or knowledge whether, for instance, did you know that, for instance, in Tarcin there was a camp?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a camp in Tarcin, the so-called Silos, and we did not do any investigation with regard to this camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about this camp Silo in Tarcin? What nationality were the people who were imprisoned in the camp?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we have ventured quite far from the subject matter. Why don't you ask me about Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking you to answer. If you cannot answer, then say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, may I remind you that if a question is put to you and if for whatever reason you think that it would be an improper question, please do not start any debate with Defence counsel. If there's anything that bothers you, please address me, and we'll find out what to do. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us how often you conducted investigations in the Dobrinja area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I conducted, at most, five or six investigations in relation to shelling and sniping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "at most" in relation to Dobrinja, could you tell us if you have any knowledge whether there was a command post in Dobrinja of the 5th Motorised Brigade staff?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it probably was. Must have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you conducted investigations in Dobrinja on the 4th of February, 1994, did you know whether near the scene of the incident where you established that two projectiles had landed there, did you know that the main staff of the 5th Motorised Brigade was there, or of a battalion? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not know. We didn't have any knowledge of that. We did not know where the staff was, except we knew where the police administration was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you had any knowledge at what distance or how far was the front line in relation to the scene of the incident that you located and photographed when -- where Dobrinja is concerned?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. We did not know how far the front line was, but it was probably about a hundred or so metres from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, that part of Dobrinja, how far is it from Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That area is at least 5 or 6 kilometres -- no, I couldn't tell you for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, because my questions would continue in relation to the report, the criminal technician's report, if my colleagues are able to provide me, then I would continue. But if not, then my co-counsel would take over, and then I would later continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, have you been able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed I have been able to locate copies which I will just distribute to my friend and the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The English translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, the English translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it part of the file disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I can't see on the face of it whether it has been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Would you then please distribute also an exhibit which would then be D62.1, I think, for the English translation. Of course, it has not been premarked. Perhaps everyone can assist the Defence by doing the premarking. Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It might be of some assistance to the Court if I indicate that the actual translation of the document, D62, begins from immediately below the numbers 0026-8234 and ends on the next page at the area for the signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'd say there's a bit more in the translation than there is in the document. Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, do you have before you the document where we can see the file number 234/94?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please turn the page. Is this document -- was this document compiled on the 4th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after arriving at the premises of the criminal technicians' department, that's when it was compiled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you told us that this incident that you conducted your investigation of the site of the incident, that there was a team present there headed by the investigating judge, and I will read the first two lines of this text. And I will remind you that you told us today that on this place, the investigation was carried out regarding the landing of two projectiles. You said in your report --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in this report at 11.25 that the aggressor from their locations in Lukavica fired two projectiles of 120 millimetres to the neighbourhood of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you were reading perhaps from the original text that -- no, not from the original text. In the transcript it reads in English that two projectiles of 120 millimetres, and as far as I even can detect from the original language, it says three. And in the translation, at least it says three 120 millimetre mortar shells. So when you -- I did not hear what you said, whether you said two or not in B/C/S, but the translation says two.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has confirmed that he investigated on the 4th of February, 1994, the scene in Dobrinja where the incident happened and where two mortar shells fell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're quoting the -- yes, the transcript. I have not, perhaps, been attentive enough. You're quoting the transcript and not the report. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Sorry, page 60, line 2, it says -- the question says: "You said in this report, you said in this report at 11.25 that the aggressor from their locations in Lukavica fired two projectiles." But according to the translation at least, and I think the original three projectiles are mentioned. That's what we have to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm for us that you said that at the site where you conducted investigation with the Judge Eterovic's team, that you answered my question that it was an incident involving two mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said we investigated the case of two mortar shells having landed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After that, I read out to you the report of the criminal investigation of the site which you identified, and beneath Item 4 where the text begins, "On the 4th of February, 1994, at 11.25, the aggressor fired three mortar shells from its position at Lukavica." Did you note this?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we noted and wrote this down. However, the third shell fell a block of buildings outside this site where we investigated these two shells. And as I said, the priority task of these investigations was the site of these two projectiles because there were more casualties, more, that is, fatalities and people injured. The third projectile did not cause injuries so we did not investigate it. And the photo documentation and the recording was done only with regard to these two mortar shells which killed nine people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will show you, from the photo documentation given us by the Prosecution relative to the incident of the 4th of February, 1994, photograph number 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Besic, will you look at the photograph number 9. You do not have photograph number 9 before you.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Markale. This is Markale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photograph for the 4th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's P2247.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you have before you photograph number 9. Did you photograph this site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer for us, in this part where you say a 120 millimetre shell fell, did you find a stabiliser there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where was the stabiliser in this place?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stabiliser here was here, there is an arrow marking it. So it was here. You can't really see the arrow properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You merely noted the point -- place of impact. You did not say that a stabiliser had been found there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in relation to this point where were the shrapnel pieces? Were there any?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pieces were in this area here where you can see the damage. You can see here the damage done to the walls, and some earth which was thrown against this wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, the witness on photograph number 9 explains or rather clarifies that in the place number 1 where the stabiliser was found, the stabiliser of a shell, and in relation to the window and the darkened part next to the window, and the part which is looking from -- to the left with certain damage to the material, is built, he is explaining that this is where the pieces of the shrapnel were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if it was recorded officially, that the stabiliser and shell shrapnel were found in this part?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who on your team noted about this part, what was there on the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a record which the judge makes. It is his record which says that the point of impact of the shell was here, that there were pieces of the shell, and the projectile itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you told us that in this part of Dobrinja, there were two more sites which you identified as the place which had been hit by the mortar shells, did you also find for these two places the shell stabilisers or mines?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the platform which we investigated two mortar projectiles. In this photo documentation is the documentation for these two projectiles. The investigation of the site of impact of the third projectile was not done. If you look at the front of the photograph number 1, you'll be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to look at the photograph number 1 and tell us in relation to these two sites where you identified these two sites, where is it that you didn't conduct the investigation?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph, you can see -- this is a broad view of the area where the investigation is conducted. There are no photographs of the impact point of the third projectile which fell -- which landed in a residential block behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer for us for which of these three incidents which we have identified here, and you marked them, which of the incidents you did not investigate, on this photograph or on photograph number 9?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. This documentation was done only for the two projectiles which landed here. The third projectile fell a block of buildings beyond, that is, beyond the range of this area. And it is not in this area at all, the third projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Besic, you are confirming for us that this photograph, number 9, reflects the site where a mortar mine fell which is marked and which can be seen on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used a marker to -- yesterday -- to mark the place where the second mortar projectile landed. It is this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that this is the site, the one that we see on photograph number 9?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, this third projectile, in which street did it land?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: West. Looking from here, from this direction, to the west of it. That is, the next block of buildings over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't that part of the site sketched and who made the sketch?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samir Salman did the sketch, and it shows where and on what street the third projectile landed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the name of the street is?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to this photograph, can you tell us where is the police station?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: North of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think I really could tell you the name of the street. It used to be Mitsubishi Avenue in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if this third projectile landed on the ground?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: We never investigated the third projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Then on the basis of what did you write "three mortar mines?"

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of statements by witnesses who were present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the time when you wrote this criminal report, you wrote three mortar shells without checking the third site about which you tell us that that is where the fall of the mine occurred?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We thought that a priority was to investigate this place where a number of people suffered and were killed so that when we completed that part of our work, as the day was drawing to a close, we did not go out to the point of impact of the third shell because there were no injured -- because there were no casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, can you tell us if when writing the report you had any knowledge of what the ballistics report looked like?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the text. I did not, however, know how they drew it up. I did not participate in the drawing up of the ballistic report. It was done by Sabljica and Cevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that no sooner did you complete the investigation than the communication was issued about the incident, and they also gave the opinion as to the direction from which it was fired?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was done on site, as in the previous case, that is the map of the city was placed there. It was guarded. And the direction was determined from which the projectile had been fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, being it's five minutes -- 25 minutes to 6.00, could you find within the next one or two minutes a suitable moment to stop so that we have another break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to this incident, I'd like to -- I'd like you to answer us: In which part of this photograph, photograph 1, did you identify the site where the largest number of casualties were?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this part, this part here. This area right here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, the Defence wishes it to be written down that witness, on photograph number 1, identifies the area marked with an arrow as the site of the incident where there was the largest number of victims. And I believe this is a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. We'll adjourn until 5 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph number 1, you located or you indicated two places about which you said where you conducted the investigation. You said that you did not do the investigation of the third site.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to these two places, how far away was the site where the third projectile landed in relation to these first two places, how far is the third one?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was about 50 metres, perhaps maybe 70.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you tell us now that you did not go to this third site to do the investigation, could you answer on the basis of what did you say three mortar shells in your report?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived to the site of the incident, we found several witnesses who told us that three projectiles had landed. So one landed one block behind, and the two projectiles landed there. So it was on the basis of the witnesses, of what they said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether your colleague who you said did a sketch, did he also mark on that sketch the place of the third projectile?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did, and he did go there, and he went and he did it. He did a sketch, but I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Sabljica, who was a ballistic expert, and Mr. Mededovic, did they go to that third site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they did. I don't think they went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you confirm that in your report, you put three mortar shells, three 120-millimetre mortar shells, and you confirmed that you went to two investigations. And for the third, for the third shell, you just wrote it in your report of basis of witness statements?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in your job description, the job that you do -- the work that you do, is it allowed for you to write something in your report, to write about such incidents on the basis of witness statements without checking it out, without corroborating it, saying it was a shell?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering that the investigating Judge Eterovic was present, he put it in his report, in his record, and I presume that investigating Judge Zdenko did see the site and probably established that it was not necessary to do an investigation of the third site. But in the record it was established that three projectiles had landed, three shells, three grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Besic, there's just another question I'd like to ask. In the course of making -- writing your report about the investigation, the criminal technicians' report of the site of the incident regarding the Markale incident, when you submitted your report, did you also have in mind the ballistic experts' report done by Mrs. Sabljica and Mr. Cavcic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have the opportunity to read it, but I did not participate in the making of the report because I did not take part in that part of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you have this opportunity to read it, after how many days?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that in your report, criminal technician's report, which was shown to you by my colleagues, you stated that on that day, there was a shelling from the aggressors' position. On the basis of what did you write that report? What data, on the basis of which data?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was on the basis of the arrow which indicated the direction from which the mortar shell came. This is from the area of Lukavica, area which is -- area which is in the easterly direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you wrote your report, the criminal technician's report, you wrote that the shell was fired from the agressors' positions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just as a matter of clarification, Mr. President, I'm wondering if the previous response of the witness or the question was referring to the incident of the 5th of February or to the incident of the 4th of February, if that could just be clarified, which incident was counsel referring to in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I understood Ms. Pilipovic well, she was referring to the report which states on that date there was shelling from the aggressors' positions, I think she was still referring to the report of the 4th of February. But if I'm wrong, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. This is the report I'm talking about, for the 5th of February, the incident I'm referring to is about Markale.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then you did not ask me the question properly if we're talking about the shelling of Dobrinja, then we should have stressed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about the incident report in Markale.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not mention the location or the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now show you the report in a sufficient number of copies for you in English, and I would ask you to read -- or I could read you this part of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, let me just try to clarify. Is the report that you are distributing now -- oh, that's P2309, which is it right that it's already tendered by the Prosecution? Even the Prosecution's number is on it. Is there any reason, do you want to have any markings made on it, or is it just -- I mean, you can just ask the Registrar to show the witness already --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...So then perhaps D65 should then be returned in order to avoid whatever confusion, and the witness should be shown P2309, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you identified this report during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the report, the date is 5th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when did you compile this report?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was compiled -- the report was compiled on Sunday, because I was called by the chief to finish the report. And the photo file was then on the 7th, because the lab, the photo lab, couldn't finish their work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're telling us that this report was written after the photographs were finished?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, before the photographs. After arriving from the investigation, the investigation is logged, and they are numbered in the record number. This is what the number is here, the book number, 240/93. It's just an error. It should be 94. After that, we type up the criminal technicians' report, and then a photo lab photos are done, and then the following day we finish the photo file.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were compiling this report of yours, did you also have a ballistic's report?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I was not -- I did not have the opportunity to see it on the same day, but I saw it on Monday, on Tuesday. When everything was gathered together, I had an opportunity to see the ballistic's report which was then made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us on the basis of which did you write that it was from the agressors' positions that the shelling of the city was carried out on that day?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the position, that is, the front lines, the demarcation lines were quite far away. And the direction was established after the arrow was placed showing the direction, and the direction was Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're confirming that you wrote your report on the basis of placing of the arrow, which we were able to identify on the photographs, and that is what your answer is?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honour, the cross-examination will be continued by my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, proceed. You'll further be cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin, counsel for the Defence, Mr. Besic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good afternoon. Thank you for being in this courtroom. I will ask you a number of questions, and I will attempt every time to be as specific as possible in relation to what we'll be talking about. The first question is -- refers to sniping. You said that you did a number of investigations that were to do with sniping, and I presume that this is the principal that you can confirm for us. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. So when we were doing such investigations, and when we are using the string or a tube technique, could you please confirm the existence of such techniques, the tube and the string?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are such measures. With a string, we can connect two or a number of -- or a number of points. We can also connect to several other points with a tube. And what happens, that can happen, is that the bullet or the projectile first hits a glass. If we're talking about double glass, for instance, it goes to one glass, and then it cannot break the second layer of glass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I believe that you have a certain expertise in this. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then tell us, what are the standards that you are using, or the criteria, to take into consideration the necessary modification, the alteration of the projectory of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it please you, Mr. President, notwithstanding that the witness said that he did have - to use my friend's word as translated - "a certain expertise", a certain expertise in the area of using strings or tubes, the witness has clearly demarcated the area of his expertise, what he is trained to do in criminal investigations and what he can speak about in terms of his training. And it might not be helpful to the Court for him to be speaking about matters outside of his training and expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the first thing we have to establish is whether the question was within the expertise -- the question was about a matter within the expertise or outside the expertise. Would you please, first, then, ask that to the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, so, in effect, during your work, your professional experiences, did you have a task to find out where a projectile could come from, one or several?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about a small calibre ammunition, for instance, a rifle, what we do in the investigation, in an investigation of a site, we are just connecting two points that could possibly indicate the direction where the projectile or the bullet came from. So by linking up these two points, one point could be inside a room, and the second point could be in the glass, or the third, if there is one, so for instance, if there is a cover outside or a roof outside of the building. So this is only the direction of the bullet of the trajectory, where it came from. In those cases, if it is not possible to link up these two points, then we do not say that we can determine where the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that according to what the witness just said, I believe that I can now ask the question that I wanted to ask. Do I have your authorisation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm also looking to Mr. Stamp, because it's not quite clear to me whether the question you've put to the witness really brings us any further as far as his expertise is concerned. Let me try to do it more directly. Mr. Besic, you've told us about a system of connecting two points in order to establish where a small projectile came from. Did you have any knowledge and do you take into account when you're working that a bullet usually does not fly in a direct line, but makes a trajectory which is not a straight line from the point where fired to the point where it lands? Do you take it into account? Have you any knowledge of this phenomenon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Normally every bullet loses some force as it is fired; and after a certain time, it does fall, so there is a landing angle. Of course, it's not a straight line. It loses its speed, its force, and the force is lower. And of course, there is a slight fall. In this case, because we are talking about short distances --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, my question was whether you take this into account while establishing the source of the fire in general. Do you do some mathematics on that part as well? Have you specific knowledge, apart from the global knowledge that you have, and what criteria would you use? What methods would you use to calculate this phenomenon in your findings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't have training like that. We didn't do any calculations. This is only determining two points and determining where the projectile came from. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I expect that this will give you enough guidance to know where the expertise of the witness is and where it might not be. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, but I have a third question in this field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you conducted these investigations, is it possible to have ricochets, as they are called, when a projectile is fired?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, there is ricochet. So a bullet or a projectile which comes to an obstacle then changes its direction, its trajectory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. So it is theoretically possible that a projectile which would go through the very first obstacle, which is more or less solid or consistent, it could deviate to the right or to the left. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. In fact, if we're talking about a bullet or about shrapnel, if it comes to an obstacle, it is possible that it will change its course, whether to the left or to right. But it is then possible to see a deformation on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So the deformation could go up to it being actually broken up?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases, it does happen. It depends on the obstacle. It could burst. But in most cases, no. That happens quite rarely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. And I believe that I'm making myself clear that we're talking about deviations to the left or to the right, so any direction in space. It is possible, to the left and to the right; also, it can go up or down.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does depend on the obstacle that it encounters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. We agree. Thank you, Witness. Now, since we clarified these points, I would like to go back to some other questions. I would like to go back to the questions regarding Markale. You told us that the photographer was with you. I am not sure that I remember his name. Could you give us the name of the cameraman, the man who was manning the videocamera?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatan Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, Witness, he filmed the entire scene, the entire site, what we saw yesterday - I'm talking about on site - on Markale site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he filmed all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He did it with the same camera?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the same camera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, now I'm going to go back to the chronology of the events and the photographs. But first of all, I would like you to tell us whether there were operations on site. I'm talking about the Markale site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The objection really is vagueness. "Operation on site", it could lead us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had some difficulties because I changed channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question is about operations on site. Witness could take us anywhere. The question I object to, it is too vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please be more precise, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was clearer in French. But by "operations", what I meant of course, I meant surgical -- I meant surgery, surgical operations.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. What do you mean "surgery"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see with your own eyes that there were surgical operations, surgeries, on site trying to sewing up injuries, tending to the wounds?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not done on site. The conditions were not such to do that on site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for your answer. So you are absolutely certain there were no surgical operations on the Markale site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer because I wasn't on site immediately. I arrived about 35, 45 minutes after it happened, to the site of the incident. We didn't find any people or corpses or the wounded. We found the space that was secured, as I explained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. As far as you know, was there a medical facility on site, a kind of field medical facility on site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was nothing like that on site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at this time, I would like to have a look at the video that we saw yesterday, and I've already informed the technical booth. This is the P29 -- 2278. And if it is possible, we could just stop to have a look at it, and then I can say when the projection will actually start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the technical booths --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we just clarify the number. Is it P2278 or P2279?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's at least what my understanding in French is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could tell us because he has it in his hands. [In English] Please check the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is 2278.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is my recollection correct when I say that 2278 was the incomplete version, and 2279 was the complete version of the tape, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. May I have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We had two versions of the tape, one more or less redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I express my understanding. I think the version shown earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- which was an extract was 2279. What was shown later we have designated 2279A, and that is a Court original or part thereof. What I think is being tendered up now is something which we disclosed to the Defence but has not yet been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a tape --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's a tape we have not seen yet in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anything else on that tape compared to the tapes we have seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may describe what the tape depicts, it really shows the scene of Markale before the police arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The wounded and dead casualties being removed from the scene, and it shows aspects of a hospital. This tape was intended to be tendered through a witness who was on scene before the police arrived. And I think we did indicate that to the Defence. But I think that is where the confusion has arisen. This has not yet been put in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what Mr. Stamp tells us, that this is not the video that we saw yesterday. Is that correct? And is this number 2278?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that this is a tape which originates from the Prosecution, which is the summary of what the Prosecution wanted to put in its case. And I thought it would be useful to see it. But perhaps if we could go back to the witness tomorrow and then have a look at the video together, if -- I don't know what Mr. Stamp would like us to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you introduced the videotape you were about to play, is that what you said, "Mr. President, at this time I would like to have a look at the video that we saw yesterday, and I have already informed the technical booth, and that is...", and you came up with the number 2278. But that is not the video we saw yesterday. Am I correct in my understanding? Because that's what Mr. Stamp tells us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. First of all, I'm sorry about yesterday; we only saw just smoke yesterday. But we are talking about Monday. This cassette is most probably the summary of what we saw, what we saw in the course of Monday. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Mr. Stamp has explained to us that we have -- that there are two videotapes used on Monday, one is the complete version of - let me say the police videotape; I'm just putting it short - and a redacted one, just showing portions of it. Initially, the Prosecution thought they could do with the redacted version, but finally it turned out that they needed all the information on the tape. So I think finally they will only tender the complete version. But these both were police tapes. What you are about to present to this Court is, in your own words, the tape of yesterday - and of course, we are talking about the day before yesterday - but is not the police video. Am I correct in my understanding? Because I now understand far better a few of your questions, perhaps. But would you please be clear on whether you are replaying a video or part of a video we've already seen, or that you're playing a video which has been disclosed to you by the Prosecution as a totally different kind of video. This means a video, as explained by Mr. Stamp, a video made by someone before the police arrived. Am I correct in my understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is quite correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you be quite clear on that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Are we playing the police video we have seen already, or are we playing a totally different video?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel's microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we should see this tape, but there is no time. But we shall do it tomorrow when we proceed. We shall have to see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I want a clear answer from you whether the tape you asked to be played. Whether it will be played now or not is a different question. I want a clear answer whether the tape you presented us is a tape --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the tape back, and then I will ask the witness a direct question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just put a question to you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I'd like to have an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to confer with my colleague. Thank you

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a tape which we received on Saturday, Mr. President, and therefore it is obviously an integral tape. But we shall now confirm it. We received this tape on Saturday, and chronologically the answer has been provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, has a tape with a number 2278 been provided to the Defence last Saturday?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was disclosed to them on the 27th of February. They might have received it or picked it up on Saturday, but it was disclosed on the 27th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How was it indicated to the Defence that this was not, as I call it, the police video?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was indicated because it bore a different number. And whereas the police video would have been referenced to this witness, Sead Besic, this other video was referenced to another witness, Esad Hadzimuratovic, on our letter of a date I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I look at -- you're talking about Hadzimuratovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Hadzimuratovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hadzimuratovic. On my last list, I see as exhibit numbers mentioned for Esad Hadzimuratovic only 3121, not 2278.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On a letter addressed to the counsel for the Defence and copied to this Chamber dated the 27th of February, we sent by fax to the Defence and filed it immediately for Court, we indicate in the second paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just find it first, Mr. Stamp. You said a letter of the?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 27th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 27th. Yes, I have it. Yes, I have here a letter of the 27th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I refer to the second paragraph, Mr. President. And I did make an error. It was not disclosed on the 14th of March -- it was not disclosed on the 27th of February. The 27th of February is the date of the letter. It was, in fact, disclosed on the 14th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it was approximately one year ago. And where does it clearly now indicate that this is not a police video? Is this from the list of exhibits? Can we see it there? I haven't got a list of exhibits. Could you please read for us entry 2278, which should not be too difficult? Have you got a list? No, it's not the list of exhibits tendered into evidence but the exhibit list that has been filed in accordance with Rule 65 ter. That means the long list of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the exhibit list, it reads "2278".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And video in respect of the shooting of Sarajevo market, Markale, 5 February, 1994. And it is -- the ERN number is V000-0350 disclosed on the 14th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what does it read on 2279?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 2279 is excerpt of videotape, and I'll ask you to forgive my B/C/S. It's a quotation from B/C/S. Labelled "Mati Grejala Obseja Za Otegrevaca, Genocide 1, Rane Zude Ena, CSB Sarajevo, Markale" [phoen]. CSB Sarajevo is a reference to the police department. Acronym in B/C/S to the police department. But the two tapes bear different evidence numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. But you indicated, and it was of importance for this Chamber to find out, and it must have been clear to you, whether there was any risk of anyone in this courtroom being misled by the type of video that would be played. That's the reason why I put the questions to Mr. Piletta-Zanin. And I did that also on the basis of you saying that it has been made clear to the Defence that this was not a police -- not a police exhibit, not a police video, as I just said short. I now do understand that from the quotation in B/C/S, in the number and the absence of such quotation in 2278, it should have been clear that it was a different type of video. Well, at least now it's clear to me what you meant by saying that it was indicated to the Defence that this was not a police video. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you told us that it was about a video that was given to you only last weekend. Was this the redacted video, 2279, that was given to you? Because the Prosecutor tells us that approximately one year ago, 2278 has been disclosed to the Defence. Could you please clarify that. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll resolve the problem. Two videotapes I collected on Saturday from the locker when I was also given the -- got the binders under 92 bis. It is Dobrinja, the 5th of February, 1994, and the tape which I do not have now, which is here with the Registrar. In October, and I think it was October 2002 [sic], the police tape was disclosed to the witness -- to the Defence which the witness identified, and it is 3274.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My English translation says October 2002. That's perhaps a bit too futuristic for this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why it says 2002, when the Prosecution disclosed all the video evidence. That evidence including a tape, which said a videotape, police report of 5th February, 1994, Markale, Markale market. And I'd like to ask our learned friends to tell us what video evidence do they have in their possession?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just give me one second to read again what has been said. Ms. Pilipovic, you told us that you collected -- one of the two videotapes you collected last weekend from your locker was a video concerning the 5th of February, 1994. Was that Number 2279 or was that 2278, or was that 2279A?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the tape which I have now is 3822. That is what I collected on Saturday and the tape which is now ready to be shown. That is what I collected on Saturday. Now, I do not know what the number is, and I do not know who has the tape. So they might tell us the number. The tape says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just see the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The two videos that are with the Registry at this moment are 2279 and the second one, 2279A. The third one, which was in the hands of the usher, is exhibited number P2278. And it reads: "Extract from V000 or VODO" - I can't read that properly - "0350 pertaining to Markale shelling." So that's the video of which you say, Mr. Stamp, that it's a video made not by any police force?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not by any police force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not by any police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may clarify one other thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The other tape which was put into counsel's locker, which she just referred to, was one which from the evidence Mr. Besic said he brought in very recently and which this Court sometime last week directed us to give a copy to the Defence immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But this video has not yet been shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: P2278 has not yet been shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but that's the -- is that the video in the locker? Because this is the one, 2278, which has been disclosed you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Last year. We gave them another copy, as the letter of the 27th indicates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's for convenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's for convenience. That's the letter of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 27th. And the letter goes on, "Another new video exhibit that we received recently is also being listed and planned to be tendered through Mirza Sabljica. We are also placing this video in your locker."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp, you are requested to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The difficulty really arises in respect of the tape which was just produced by my friend. That tape was clearly designated as a different tape from what has been shown before in the Court by the number, the exhibit number, and the ERN number, and the description on the exhibit list. They are different tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you say is you provided, just for the convenience of the Defence, a video, P2278, which you additionally were planning to tender through Witness Esad Hadzimuratovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand this. I do not understand why this video does not appear any more on the -- among the exhibits indicated in your letter of the 6th of March, which is of -- if I look at the 6th of March, it's the most recent one. If I look at the potential exhibits for witnesses of the 6th to the 15th of March, 2002, I see Esad Hadzimuratovic. I only see one exhibit, 3121.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the letter of the 6th of March, if I may respond to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the third paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see, it has disappeared from Mr. Hadzimuratovic, but it appears with another witness. It's additional information. It's clear to me. Thank you for assisting me and better understanding where this exhibit, how it changed from Mr. Hadzimuratovic to another witness. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I simply do not know if my presence was still of any use in this Court, and I can only see that the time is passing. And that now, it is literally impossible to go through this tape regardless of its origin, and therefore I suggest that we return to it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber agrees that it would be wise to start tomorrow. You can put whatever questions on this video. At least it has been clarified now, I hope at least, or perhaps by questioning it might not be clear at all. I do not know. But one thing is for sure, as far as I can see, this is not a video we have seen before. I think that's the only thing we possibly could establish at this very moment, and we heard from the Prosecution what in the view of the Prosecution is the origin of this video. And whenever you have any other view, perhaps rather let you first question the witness and then see what comes out. Where would you like it to be kept until tomorrow morning? I think you would like it to be returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] We will see that tomorrow. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We still have a few minutes left, if there are other subjects which would not take up much -- yes. Please proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may continue my cross-examination for about 5 minutes, I shall do so gladly. If not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's wiser. I promised Mr. Stamp five minutes on another issue. So perhaps this confusion --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] He already had five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but not on the subject he asked for five minutes for. Mr. Besic, you have seen there has been a lot of confusion about just what about what video will be played to you. Looking backwards, it might have been wiser to have this debate not in your presence. Let me say this to you: Whenever a video may be played tomorrow for you, the parties may have different views as to the origin of the video. None of these visions is as it is now been established for this Chamber. I'd like you to keep that clearly in mind when you return tomorrow morning and answer whatever questions on a video when it will be played to you. I'll ask the usher now to lead you out of the courtroom since we need another five minutes to discuss another issue not related to your testimony. Would you please return tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Yes, Mr. Usher, would you please lead --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, Mr. President and Your Honours, at the beginning of today's sitting you had indicated, Mr. President, that there was some areas that need to be clarified in respect to the status of certain witnesses, whether they are experts or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have to confess that as far as the 65 ter summaries are concerned, perhaps the expression "expert" has not been used in a way that strictly confines it to Rule 94 bis. It has been used rather loosely. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And for the time being, I'd like to clarify the status in respect of the witness Mirza Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, just for this one witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour had referred to quite a number of witnesses, and we will clarify all of them in due course. But this one is one scheduled to testify soon. He is here. Everything relevant to his testimony has been served on the Defence for quite some time now, and they have been notified that he is to testify soon. He, as is indicated by the 65 ter summary, is a -- or was a police officer with specialist training in a particular field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He is not an expert for the purposes of Rule 94 bis. He, like many other police officers who are trained in a particular area of investigations, will certainly have over the years gained expertise and experience in a particular area that he can testify upon. But he is primarily a fact witness. He participated in the investigation, made observations of fact, and on the basis of his training as a police officer, he is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's quite clear to us. You regard him as a normal witness and as a witness which potentially could -- Rule 94 bis could be applied upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, any observation you'd like to make after this clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was about to say that in view of what the Prosecution says, I'd really like to answer, but there is no time to do so. I need to consult with my colleague, and perhaps we shall do so, that is, respond tomorrow if all goes well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But let me just see. We asked for a clarification to the Prosecution in order to be sure whether we are dealing with a witness or an expert witness to which Rule 94 bis might apply or not. I wonder if you would agree with the Prosecution, I wonder whether the Defence could force the Prosecution to qualify one of their witnesses as an expert. It's a question. I'm just putting it as a question. But I'm wondering if that's the issue you want to think over overnight, I'm curious to hear what you'd like to say about it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are a number of things that we can do overnight, Mr. President, and that could be one of the things that we wish to clarify. However, what we wish to clarify is how many times -- and I know how Prosecution is precise in what he wants to do, how often they have called people witnesses and at times expert witnesses. I do not have my whole file here, but I chose to remind that the letonical (phoen) system that we were made access to does not function, and we have to simply check for this witness and for other witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, well you feel that this Chamber also needed some clarification on this point. Being it's 7.00 now, we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
